subject: Order Form SLA: uptime ladder, credit formula, and patch cadence
messages:
From: Emily Lang <elang@aurorasystems.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Patel <mpatel@aurorasystems.com>, procurement@aurorasystems.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form SLA redlines and proposed maintenance carveouts

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is Aurora's redline against the MSA + Order Form focused on SLA and support: uptime targets, credit formulas, and maintenance windows (see attachment: Aurora_MSA_SLA_Redlines.pdf). Key asks from our side:

- Uptime at 99.99% for production APIs (monthly measurement), with a defined credit ladder for each 0.1% below the target.
- Credit calculation tied to affected service fees (not full invoice) and paid as credits on the next invoice.
- Scheduled maintenance limited to a weekly 4-hr window; large patches ( >1 hour ) require 72-hour notice and alignment on rollback policy.
- Initial response / escalation times: P1 within 30 minutes, P2 within 2 hrs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these positions or propose counter language? Also please confirm who on your side will own the legal redline loop so we can exchange versions in a single thread. We need a final, signed order form by 17 Sep to align with our procurement calendar.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Emily
Emily Lang
Head of Procurement
Aurora Systems

Attachment: Aurora_MSA_SLA_Redlines.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Lang <elang@aurorasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form SLA redlines and proposed maintenance carveouts

Hi Emily — appreciate the clear asks and the file. Looping in our legal and ops leads so we can consolidate a single counterproposal. Quick high-level on feasibility from the account side:

- Uptime: We can propose a two-tier approach. For Hosted customers (standard): 99.95% monthly. For Dedicated/Reserved capacity customers: 99.99% monthly. We will outline a credit ladder tied to--and capped by--monthly fees for the affected service.
- Credit cap: we typically cap credits to prevent unlimited exposure. We will propose a capped formula; legal will propose specific language.
- Maintenance: Proposed regular patch window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (4 hours). For larger patches (>1 hour impact), Redwood can provide 72 hours notice and we will coordinate a rollback plan, but we need to keep emergency maintenance carveouts for critical security fixes.
- Response times: Our ops SLA for P1 is an initial response within 1 hour and P2 within 4 hours. We understand Aurora's desire for faster times; Marissa/legal and I will confirm operational feasibility for a 30-min P1.

I'll attach our initial redline so legal can mark up (RW_redline_orderform_v1.pdf). Can we target a follow-up on Tuesday 16 Sep to exchange final positions so we can meet your 17 Sep deadline? If earlier, we can do a 30-minute sync.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: provide legal positions on credit cap and measurement.
- Laura/Aditya: confirm ops acceptability of P1 30-min or provide rationale for 1 hour.
- Priya: schedule sync with Aurora if needed.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priya@redwood.com

Attachment: RW_redline_orderform_v1.pdf (PDF, 9 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Aurora redlines — legal positions and suggested edits

Priya / team — reviewed Aurora's redline (see Emily's message below). My high-level positions and suggested language (internal only):

1) Measurement and uptime definition
- Insist on clearly scoped "Service" definition (only API endpoints listed in Order Form). Avoid account-wide uptime obligations.
- Measurement period: rolling 30-day window looks reasonable; avoid calendar-month ambiguity.

2) Credit ladder & cap
- Accept a tiered credit ladder, but cap aggregate credits to the lesser of: (i) 3x the monthly fees for the affected service, or (ii) 50% of the invoice in the affected month. This prevents runaway liability while providing meaningful remedy.
- Credits should be applied against future invoices only; Redwood will not issue cash refunds except by exception.

3) Scheduled maintenance & notice
- We can accept a 72-hour notice requirement for non-emergency maintenance >1 hour, and propose a default window (Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Add an exception for emergency security maintenance with immediate remediation rights; require post-facto notification within 8 hours for such emergency actions.

4) Response & escalation SLAs
- We should push back on a 30-minute P1 initial response. Proposed Redwood standard: P1 initial response 1 hour; P1 remediation target based on severity and root cause (we can propose a separate SLO appendix for faster remediation commitments for Dedicated customers).

5) Measurement exclusions & Customer-caused incidents
- Add explicit carveouts for incidents caused by customer configuration, third-party providers, or network issues outside Redwood's control.

6) Remedy mechanics & dispute resolution
- Require a 30-day dispute period before credits are auto-applied; include a tech contact for evidence sharing (support bundle, traces).

Please confirm operations alignment on response windows and confirm whether we have product reasons to accept a higher uptime for Dedicated customers. If legal positions above look OK, I will prepare a redline to send back to Aurora (recommended: keep credits capped as above and require DocuSign for the final Order Form).

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Lang <elang@aurorasystems.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form SLA redlines and proposed maintenance carveouts — Redwood positions and next steps

Hi Emily / Michael — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Below is a concise summary of positions Redwood can accept and the one item that still needs a short confirmation. If that all looks good we can exchange a final redline and push to DocuSign.

Accepted / agreed (Redwood -> Aurora)
- Two-tier uptime: Hosted: 99.95% (rolling 30-day); Dedicated/Reserved: 99.99% (rolling 30-day).
- Tiered credit ladder tied to the affected service fees. Credits applied only to future invoices (no cash refunds as a standard).
- Maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC as Redwood's regular patch cadence. Non-emergency maintenance >1 hour will have 72 hours notice.
- Emergency security patches: Redwood may perform immediate remediation with post-facto notification within 8 hours.
- Measurement exclusions: customer-caused incidents and third-party network outages excluded.

Open / pending (requires confirmation)
- Credit cap mechanics: Legal (Marissa) proposed capping aggregate credits to the lesser of (i) 3x monthly fees for the affected service or (ii) 50% of the invoice for the affected month. Please confirm Aurora can accept that cap.
- Response times: Ops proposes P1 initial response within 1 hour (we can qualify faster remediation targets for Dedicated customers). If Aurora still requires a 30-min initial response for Hosted, please flag the commercial impact and we will escalate.

Next steps
1) Aurora to confirm acceptance of the credit cap language above by end-of-day 17 Sep.
2) If accepted, Marissa will send a single consolidated redline and we will route to DocuSign (DocuSign link will be provided).
3) If Aurora needs the 30-min P1 for Hosted, we'll schedule a short commercial call to discuss trade-offs (discount or tier upgrade).

Attached: RW_SLA_summary_for_Aurora_20250910.pdf (summary of positions). DocuSign envelope will be created once you confirm the cap.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
